🇲🇽✊ MEXICO'S NATIONAL LOTTERY HONORS THE BATTLE THAT BROKE A DICTATORSHIP

112 years ago, on June 23, 1914, Francisco Villa's División del Norte — alongside General Felipe Ángeles and Pánfilo Natera — stormed Zacatecas and shattered the army of usurper Victoriano Huerta, hastening the dictator's collapse. Mexico's National Lottery is now dedicating its Sorteo Mayor to that battle. Its director, Olivia Salomón, said the Toma de Zacatecas "transcended the military sphere to become a symbol of resistance and transformation."

🇲🇽🇻🇪 MEXICO SENDS 250 TROOPS AND RESCUE TEAMS TO EARTHQUAKE-HIT VENEZUELA

While Washington tightens sanctions on Caracas, Mexico sends rescuers. President Sheinbaum dispatched 250 Defense Ministry personnel, four aircraft, drones, canine units and medical equipment to Venezuela after twin earthquakes (magnitudes 7.2 and 7.5) killed at least 188 people on June 24. "There are no reports of affected, injured or deceased Mexican citizens," she confirmed — the mission is pure solidarity with a neighbor in mourning.

🇲🇽⚽ A MEXICAN WOMAN JUST REFEREED A MEN'S WORLD CUP MATCH FOR THE FIRST TIME

Katia Itzel García became the first Mexican — and the first Latin American woman — to work as center referee in a men's World Cup match, officiating the Netherlands' 3-1 win over Tunisia in Kansas City. A UNAM political-science graduate and FIFA referee since 2019, she's only the fourth woman in the tournament's history to take the whistle.

🇲🇽🗳️ MEXICO'S INE APPROVES TWO NEW PARTIES — AND BLOCKS TWO FOR DARK MONEY

Mexico's electoral authority (INE) granted national registration to two new parties — PAZ and Somos México — for the 2027 elections, while denying it to "México Tiene Vida" and "Que Siga la Democracia." The reason: the Financial Intelligence Unit flagged irregular, possibly illegal financing, and one rejected group let nearly 100 clergy members actively participate — a direct breach of Mexico's church-state separation. The two approved parties each receive 84 million pesos in public financing; the dark-money projects got zero.

US MEDIA SILENCE: Sheinbaum Unveils Historic 32,000 MW Electricity Plan — 70% Renewable
June 24, 2026 | 🇲🇽

📰 Sheinbaum announced a 739-billion-peso (~$40B) plan to add 32,000 MW of capacity by 2030 — 22,000 MW (70%) renewable — lifting renewables from 23% to 38% of the national grid. 🔍 Carried by La Jornada, Mexico News Daily, BNamericas. Searched NYT, WaPo, Reuters, Bloomberg, AP: nothing.

🇲🇽 US coverage of Mexico's grid this year ran to outages and "dirty energy" — the largest clean-energy build-out in the country's history went unreported.

• Sheinbaum: "For the first time in history we have projects of 32,000 MW... and 70 percent of them are renewable"

AFP: Sheinbaum, Spanish King Use World Cup to Mend Diplomatic Rift
June 26, 2026 | 🟡

📰 AFP frames King Felipe VI's visit as Mexico and Spain mutually "mending" a rift. 🔍 What gets softened: the freeze began in 2019, when AMLO asked Spain to acknowledge conquest-era "crimes" — dismissed at the time as a stunt. The visit only happened after Felipe conceded in March there had been "a lot of abuse."

🇲🇽 Sheinbaum kept the demand and reframed it: recognizing native peoples "is a question of dignity." The king's exit tour ran past Diego Rivera's murals of the conquest.

• Sheinbaum: recognizing originary people "is a question of dignity"
• Felipe VI, March 2026: there had been "a lot of abuse" during the conquest

AP: Mexico's World Cup Joy Muted in Regions Gripped by Cartel Violence
June 26, 2026 | 🟡

📰 AP frames Mexico's World Cup as a cartel story — "celebrations that once followed big games have largely disappeared out of fear of going out at night." Its own reporting notes 100,000+ security forces deployed and Uruapan's youth filling the streets after Mexico beat South Korea.

🇲🇽 Unmentioned: Mexico logged its lowest homicide rate in 11 years in May — about 47 a day, down roughly 40% from the 2018 peak. The single official quoted at length is the US ambassador.

• "celebrations that once followed big games have largely disappeared out of fear"
• US Ambassador Ronald Johnson "lauded the collaboration between the two nations"

🇲🇽💰 <u>BANXICO FREEZES RATE AT 6.50% AS INFLATION FALLS TO 3.55%</u>

Banco de México held its benchmark rate at 6.50%, ending its cutting cycle as headline inflation fell from 4.45% to 3.55% in two months. Core inflation is the sticking point at 4.12% — 26 straight readings above 4%. Banorte expects the rate parked there through all of 2027.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>EL UNIVERSAL JOURNALIST QUITS AFTER FAKE MONSIVÁIS INTERVIEW USED TO SMEAR AMLO</u>

Edmundo Cázarez resigned from El Universal after admitting he had no audio for a "recovered" 1999 Monsiváis interview the paper republished to attack AMLO — a version that added a paragraph that didn't exist in 2024. Monsiváis's own family demanded proof or an apology. This is how the outrage machine works: print the smear first, find the receipt never.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>GDP ISN'T DEVELOPMENT — SHEINBAUM REJECTS THE NEOLIBERAL SCOREBOARD</u>

Sheinbaum dismissed GDP as "a very aggregate indicator that doesn't speak of many other things." Her proof: under AMLO, even with the 8-point COVID GDP crash of 2020, 13.5 million people left poverty and the minimum wage soared. "A country can grow 4% — and if the wealth concentrates in a few, poverty doesn't change."
